heading: How California classifies plumbing contractors

items.label: C-36 scope
items.text: CSLB's C-36 Plumbing Contractor classification reads:
items.quote: A plumbing contractor provides a means for a supply of safe water, ample in volume and of suitable temperature for the purpose intended and the proper disposal of fluid waste from the premises in all structures and fixed works.

items.label: Gas work
items.text: The classification includes gas appliances but draws a line at forced-air heating:
items.quote: All gas appliances, flues and gas connections for all systems including suspended space heating units. This does not include forced warm air units

items.label: Water heating
items.quote: Installation of any type of equipment to heat water, or fluids, to a temperature suitable for the purposes listed in this section, including the installation of solar equipment for this purpose

items.label: Safety devices
items.text: Maintenance and replacement extends to safety devices such as
items.quote: gas earthquake valves, gas control valves, back flow preventers, water conditioning equipment and regulating valves

items.label: Classes CSLB maps to C-36
items.text: On CSLB's Reciprocal Classifications List, the rows that correspond to C-36 are all Arizona classes: C-37, K-77 and L-77 (Plumbing, Including Solar) and C-37R, K-37 and L-37 (Plumbing). The Nevada, Louisiana, Mississippi and North Carolina tables have no C-36 row.

originShared.text: None of these states is one of the states CSLB reciprocates with (Arizona, Louisiana, Mississippi, Nevada, and North Carolina), so no reciprocity applies.
CSLB's NASCLA reciprocity route is for applicants for the General Building classification, so it does not cover C-36.
Apply with CSLB's Application for Original Contractor License and the $450 non-refundable application fee.

Document at least four years of journeyman-level or higher C-36 experience, obtained within the last 10 years, on CSLB's Certification of Work Experience form. The form's definition of a contractor includes an out-of-state licensed contractor.
After CSLB accepts the application, pass a trade exam and/or a business and law exam; exam fees are paid directly to the testing vendor.
